title: Policy-chosen first help versus the fixed hint-ladder start
activation: Owner decision only. Requires PRI_FEATURE_TUTOR_POLICY=1 on the server, a client build made with PRI_FEATURE_TUTOR_POLICY=1, and this id in PRI_EXPERIMENTS. Status stays 'off' in this file; the environment is the switch, so turning it on or off is a deployment change, not a code change.
prerequisites: An A/A run of the assignment and logging path (RESEARCH_TO_BUILD_V7 V7-24) with no unexplained sample-ratio mismatch, recorded before any readout of this experiment is interpreted.

The protected different-family outcome items for the skills in scope exist (DELAYED_TRANSFER_MEASUREMENT_PROTOCOL §12); until then the outcome is read on ordinary practice items of a different generator.
hypothesis: For a student who asks for help on a practice question, offering the smallest next intervention chosen by the transparent tutor policy (client/src/engine/tutorPolicy.js, tutor-policy-v1) instead of the hint ladder's fixed first rung changes the rate of delayed independent success on a different item family of the same skill. Direction is not assumed: the policy may also lower it.

arms.description: Today's practice card: the hint ladder starts at its first rung (nudge); no policy panel.
The policy panel above the same ladder offers one smallest next step with its reason. Rungs, their order, their cost and the server's charge are unchanged.

eligibility: A signed-in student account with a server-graded practice attempt (practice, review or task mode) after activation. Exam, mock, placement and every one-try mode are excluded: the policy is off there and no attempt in those modes counts.
trigger: Assignment is computed for every eligible account from a stable hash of (salt, account id) and stamped on each graded-attempt event while the experiment is active (intention to treat). Exposure to the panel is not required for inclusion.

primaryOutcome.definition: Per account, the first index attempt after assignment on skill S (dot point, else generator) whose skill has a later qualifying outcome: the first graded attempt on S from a DIFFERENT item family (generator) made at least delayHours after the index attempt, with no hint-ladder rung opened, no help requested through the help plan, not a reveal and not a repeat. Success = that outcome attempt is correct. One binary outcome per account.
primaryOutcome.independence: hintLevel 0, revealed false, repeat false, and no help requested on the item through the help plan, in either arm (policyAssistance: a request is recorded in the control arm too, so the exclusion does not depend on the arm). Tutor-panel use is device-observed and not on the event; it is a recorded limitation, not an assumption of independence.
primaryOutcome.missing: An account with no qualifying outcome is missing, never a failure. Outcome observation rates are reported per arm and checked for imbalance.

guardrails.metric: Median device-reported milliseconds per resolved graded attempt (the submit body's ms), per arm.
guardrails.harm: Policy arm median more than 1.5 times control.

guardrails.metric: Share of resolved graded attempts that are reveals (Show solution or the solution rung), per arm.
guardrails.harm: Policy arm share more than 5 percentage points above control.

guardrails.metric: Learner or guardian reports about help or hints, per arm.
guardrails.harm: Any report that the policy withheld help a student needed, reviewed by a person.

minimumSample.basis: Two-sided alpha 0.05, power 0.80, to detect a 15 percentage-point difference around a 45% base rate needs about 170 accounts with an observed outcome per arm (normal approximation); 200 allows for attrition between assignment and outcome. This is a planning figure, not a measured variance; no smaller sample is read for efficacy.

analysis.estimand: Difference in the per-account success proportion, policy minus control, among accounts with an observed outcome.
analysis.interval: Newcombe hybrid score interval (Wilson score per arm), 95%.
analysis.srm: Chi-square goodness of fit of assigned accounts against the arm weights; p < 0.001 stops interpretation until the cause is found. Outcome-observation balance is reported the same way.
analysis.stoppingRule: One fixed-horizon efficacy readout once every arm has at least minimumSample.perArm observed outcomes. Interim readouts show counts and guardrails only. Guardrails may stop the experiment for harm at any time; they never declare a winner.
analysis.decision: Promotion of the policy to all students requires the interval's lower bound to exceed zero at the fixed horizon, no guardrail breached, an A/A pass recorded, and an owner decision. A null or negative result keeps the fixed ladder.

limitations: Twelve real accounts today: this experiment cannot be read for months, and the readout refuses below the minimum sample.
The different-family outcome uses ordinary practice items until a protected outcome bank exists, so outcome items may have been seen in tutoring.
Time on task is device-reported, not server-measured.
Complaint reports have no product channel yet; the guardrail is manual until one exists.
Results transport only to Pri students who ask for help in untimed practice; nothing here is evidence about exams, other products or other populations.
claims: None. Nothing about this experiment may appear in product copy, marketing or reports as evidence that the tutor policy works, until a fixed-horizon readout meets the decision rule above.
